newsitem.title: USA: Steady growth seen for US ag exports - Goldthwait.
newsitem.headline: Steady growth seen for US ag exports - Goldthwait.

text.p: U.S. agricultural exports will experience steady growth through the year 2005, but will be faced with stiff competition, a senior agriculture department official said on Friday.

Speaking at the annual meeting of the National Grain and Feed Association, USDA's General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said, "We believe there is a good, strong basis for further growth in agricultural exports ... but the markets will be subject to intense competition."
Goldthwait said that the U.S. agricultural subsidy program -- the Export Enhancement Program -- is a necessary tool to fight unfair trade practices.
"EEP remains a valuable tool to combat unfair trade practices," he said.
Goldthwait said that USDA is puzzled by the European Union's use of subsidies for its wheat exports.
"We don't think they're buying market share. We just think they are lowering prices," he said, commenting on the EU wheat subsidies.

Goldthwait said that the United States will continue to be the dominant supplier through 2005 of global coarse grain exports. He said the agency does not expect China to return as a big presence in coarse grain exports and also predicted that European Union shipments of coarse grain will slip.

The USDA official said that the major growth markets for U.S. coarse grains and wheat would be in the developing countries of Asia and Latin America, and he also said that U.S. agricultural exports to Russia will continue to improve.
Goldthwait noted that the recent increase of exports to Russia has been "sort of a surprise," but said that Russia has been buying U.S. grain in the form of poultry imports.
Goldthwait said he expects the U.S. share of the world wheat market to recover to the 33 to 35 percent range, and remain there for "several years."
He noted that the availability of world wheat stocks is still tight and said that wheat ending stocks remain at "very, very low levels."
